r0.why: Name, Explorer 66, 1989-1993, goals, RELIKT-1, WMAP and Planck dates all in [1],[2],[6].

r1.why: Two pieces of evidence [3]; anisotropy gloss as brightness differences follows from [42]; 2006 Nobel to Mather/Smoot with affiliations [14]-[16]; precision-science quote [5].

r2.why: Faithful paraphrase of the 1 um-1 cm whole-sky aim [7] and the three measured quantities [8].

r3.why: $30M condition [9], IRAS overruns and 1981 start at GSFC [10], IRAS-like detectors/dewar [11], 1988 Shuttle plan and Challenger grounding [12], Delta 18 Nov 1989 SSO [13].

r4.why: Systematic-error design [18], 0.8 rpm for anisotropy errors [21], orbit requirements met by circular SSO [26]-[27], 900 km/99 deg [28], day-night boundary [30], shield and six-month scan [31].

r5.why: 650 L superfluid helium dewar for FIRAS/DIRBE [33], conical shield blocking Sun/Earth/radio [35], insulating blankets [36], Jan 1994 handover to WFF [37].

r6.why: DMR three radiometers at 31.4/53/90 GHz [38], microwave receivers switching between horn pair, fields 60 deg apart [40],[42], ~3E-5 K sensitivity [44].
